# Narrated amendment aftermath: report-runner retry batch

All `read` and stage actions below are narrated, not executed. No live calls are made, and no reference contents are rebuilt from memory. A `read` marked "readable" proceeds. Any required reference that is unreadable stops that path with a blocking error.

## Main trace (git)

**M1.** `read` `skills/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md`, §5 "Apply, aftermath, commit", before the aftermath. The rule forbids running this section from memory. The file is readable, so the trace proceeds.

**M2. Ledger check.** There is no line-1 `# Ledger - loop engine` in the plan dir, so this is the plan path, not the ledger bypass.

**M3. Classify the human-facing outcomes.** Both enter the attribution check:
- **Second identical `plan_check` FAIL.**
  - The quoted plan text is `` Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` ``.
  - `git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD:doc/plans/report-runner.md` shows Task 1's Tests as `` `node --test eval/lib/lint.test.mjs` baseline: 3a8fad8c pass; ... ``.
  - The text is therefore changed by this batch. Task 1's `Spec:` anchor is `#tests`, the amended section, so the FAIL is attributable.
- **First `dirtied tracked source` row.**
  - Its baseline command, `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`, is the same batch-added Tests text, so the row is also attributable.
- Neither a line number nor task membership was used as proof. There is no unrelated output, so no partition is needed.

**M4. Budget and redraw check.**
- "Run report replay" was the batch's own amend, not an aftermath item. This retry is aftermath item 1 of a maximum of 2.
- Its evidence does not repeat an applied item's evidence.
- It changes Tests only, not Goal, Problem, ACs or boundaries. It is amend-class, not a redraw.

**M5. Restore eligibility for the amend-class row.**
- Each named path is checked with `ls-files`:
  ```bash
  git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
  git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
  git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
  ```
- Each check prints its path, so all three are tracked.
- None of them is the spec, the plan, or an `In-flight:` path.
- None is a new `??` at a `Create:`/`Test:` path.
- `artifacts: /tmp/report-runner-artifacts/audit.log` lies outside the row and is preserved, not touched.

**M6. Restore exactly the eligible row's paths.** The orchestrator does this itself, one quoted path per command, before the retry applies:
```bash
git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
```
- Each command exits 0. A nonzero exit would stop the trace and print the shell error.
- This grants no general permission to restore test damage. The rest of the pre-batch tree is preserved.

**M7. Hold the item.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| handle | `replay` |
| title | Move replay to verification |
| what | the spec's Tests replay at final verification, not in Task 1 Tests |
| location | Tests |
| recommended | accept |
| alternatives | none (no `alt-n`) |
| evidence | the verbatim FAIL lines (`FAIL (1 findings)` / `command-contract @ line 24: ...` / `` > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` ``) plus the dirtied row verbatim |

**M8. Grant acknowledgment.**
- `read` `amendment-surface.md` §[Standing grants] (§1 predicate and Value decoding). It is readable.
- Re-reading the spec header observes `**Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends`. That is amend permission, not malformed and not budget-only or `none`.
- The recommended edit is applied without a menu. Tests changes from "replays in Task 1 Tests" to "replays at final verification".
- The orchestrator prints: `amended the spec: Move replay to verification - the spec's Tests replay at final verification, not in Task 1 Tests`.

**M9. Re-dispatch the plan-writer.**
- `read` `skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md` for `## Author the plan` step 3 and steps 5-6. It is readable.
- The `plan-writer` is dispatched with only these blocks:
  - `Amend:` naming section **Tests**, with the rule sentence: "preserve every task title and wave position the amendment does not touch; edit only affected anchors and tasks — fix: Tests moved back to final verification; quoting `FAIL (1 findings)` / `command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token` / `` > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` `` and the row `` Task 1: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json ``".
  - `In-flight: doc/specs/report-runner.md, doc/plans/report-runner.md`.
- The fixed observation is `PLAN WRITTEN`, and the parent `plan_check` (steps 5-6) returns PASS.

**M10. Finalize, once, after PASS.**
- **Read.** The amended plan `doc/plans/report-runner.md` is read once. This is step 7's read only: no phase completion and no `plan_tracker` init.
- **Tracker.**
  - Task 1 "W1: Validate report records" changed its anchors and was complete, so it is reopened in place: `plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: 0, status: "in_progress" })`.
  - No tasks were added or removed, so no re-`init` is needed.
  - The phase stays `implement`, so there is no `phase_tracker` call.
- **Commit.** One commit holds spec and plan together:
  ```bash
  git -C /tmp/report-worktree add -- doc/specs/report-runner.md doc/plans/report-runner.md
  git -C /tmp/report-worktree commit -q -F - -- doc/specs/report-runner.md doc/plans/report-runner.md <<'EOF'
  amend: 2 item(s) - Run report replay, Move replay to verification

  - <handle> | Run report replay | spec Tests replay in Task 1 Tests | <its recorded kind> | <its reviewer line> | <its evidence>
  - replay | Move replay to verification | the spec's Tests replay at final verification, not in Task 1 Tests | granted | not reviewed - aftermath retry under grant | <verbatim FAIL lines + dirtied row>
  "auto-apply amends"
  EOF
  ```
- Then continue the task loop on Task 1.

**M11. Audit choice kinds.**
- Under the grant, an aftermath item records `granted`.
- Without amend permission (`none`, absent, or budget-only), §2-4 render the human batch and the turn ends without re-dispatch. A later human reply would then record one of:
  - `A` records `accepted`.
  - `B`/`C` records `alt-n`. There is none here.
  - Free text records `custom(<effect>)`. If it is a redirect, it returns to the original step-6 exit with no re-dispatch over the unfixed spec.
- Only `auto-apply` and `granted` records feed the finishing digest.

**M12. Undo.**
1. Run `git -C /tmp/report-worktree revert <batch sha>`. This undoes the retry together with the batch.
2. Read `git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD^:doc/specs/report-runner.md` and pass its `**Amend-grant:**` line through the predicate.
3. If the working tree's line differs, restore that value and persist it per Standing grants before re-entering the surface.
4. The three restored source paths were never committed, so the revert does not re-dirty them.

## Variant U (independent; same pre-restore state)

- The row also names `tests/report-new.test.mjs`. `ls-files` prints nothing for it, it shows as `??`, and it is a `Create:`/`Test:` path, so the row is ineligible.
- The **entire row** goes to step 6 without partial restoration. **None of the original three paths is restored.**
- The writing-plans step-6 branch is rendered in full:
  - It states Task 1, the command `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`, the SHA, the exit and the summary. The writer reported no SHA or exit in these observations, so they are shown as missing.
  - It offers the options on their own lines: `fix-first`, `narrow`, `amend`, then `Recommendation: <option> - <reason>`.
  - It names all four dirty paths and their cause.
  - It hands the dirty paths to the human to commit, discard or move.
  - It lists retry item `replay` with its evidence.
- The flow then pauses: no restore and no re-dispatch.

## Variant P (independent)

- The row also names `doc/specs/report-runner.md`. It is tracked but protected. The same applies to the plan or any `In-flight:` path.
- The whole row goes to step 6, rendered in full exactly as in U. **None of the original three paths is restored**, and the spec is never restored.
- The flow pauses.

## Variant R (independent)

The second identical FAIL is `acceptance-scope @ line 24: report runner must also audit refund records...`. Fixing it changes the Goal and acceptance criteria, so it is **redraw-class**. The grant never covers a redraw, and the call is stated so the user can override it.

Before any restore:
1. Commit the batch as-is: the spec, plus the plan if dirty, in an `amend:` commit with the "Run report replay" record. This is batch preservation, not cleanup.
2. Hand the original three tracked dirty paths to step 6 **without restoration**, rendering that exit in full.
3. `read` `skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md` "Amending an approved spec" (readable) and take its redraw path:
   - Keep the worktree and the spec.
   - Run `plan_tracker({ action: "clear" })`, then `phase_tracker({ action: "reset" })`, then `phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "brainstorm" })`.
   - Delete `doc/plans/report-runner.md`. There is no ledger.
   - Resume at checklist step 4 with the approved spec as the draft.
   - Step 4's in-context check `read`s `reference/ticket-acceptance.md` if needed.
4. The full gate follows.

## Plain jj equivalent (one example)

This replaces the git checkout; it is not added to it:
```bash
jj -R /tmp/report-worktree restore -- 'root:"eval/report-runner/report.md"'
```
`-R` selects the repo but does not root path resolution, which stays relative to cwd. The `root:` fileset anchors the path at the workspace root.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## Main git trace

1. **Required reference re-read.** Before the aftermath, narrate a `read` of the absolute installed path to `skills/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md`, specifically section 5. The supplied rules govern the sequence below; this is not a claim that the bundled reference was read into session context. If that required read is unreadable, stop with a blocking error.

2. **Attribute the findings before repairing anything.** Compare the second parent FAIL and dirty-command row against this batch’s changed Tests section and:
   ```bash
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD:doc/plans/report-runner.md
   ```
   The fixed observation is that HEAD used the passing lint test, while the current Task 1 uses the replay command introduced through this batch’s Tests amendment. Task 1’s `Spec:` anchor points to that amended section. This establishes attribution through changed text—not merely task membership or line 24. The missing `Test:` token alone would not justify changing the spec; the attributable replay command and its source mutations support the proposed correction.

3. **Hold one aftermath item.** Its fields are:
   - **Handle:** `replay`
   - **Title:** Move replay to verification
   - **Location:** Tests
   - **Change:** `replays in Task 1 Tests` → `replays at final verification`
   - **Recommendation:** accept; no alternatives
   - **Evidence:**
     ```text
     FAIL (1 findings)
     command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token
     > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`

     - Task 1: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json
     ```
   This is an amend-class Tests correction, not a redraw or descope: Goal, Problem, ACs, and component boundaries remain unchanged. It is the first aftermath item, not an additional independent batch.

4. **Check eligibility, then restore exactly the eligible row.** The narrated membership checks are:
   ```bash
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
   ```
   Each fixed observation prints its named path. All three are outside the spec, plan, and In-flight protections. Before applying the retry, the intended restores are:
   ```bash
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
   ```
   Each is observed to succeed with exit 0. Preserve `/tmp/report-runner-artifacts/audit.log`; it is outside this row. A nonzero restore would instead stop the sequence and report its shell error.

5. **Re-check the grant before applying.** Narrate the required `read` of Standing grants in the absolute installed amendment-surface reference, then the spec’s grant line. The fixed re-read observes:
   ```text
   **Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends
   ```
   Apply the reference’s predicate and Value decoding; unreadable reference or malformed grant means stop. This is amendment permission, not merely a fix-round budget, so the recommended amend applies without a human batch menu.

   Intended edit: restore Tests to “replays at final verification.” Confirmation:
   ```text
   amended the spec: Move replay to verification - replay runs at final verification rather than in Task 1 Tests.
   ```

6. **Re-dispatch only the affected planning work.** Narrate the required read of writing-plans’ Author-the-plan instructions. The intended `plan-writer` task contains only:
   ```text
   Amend:
   - doc/specs/report-runner.md, Tests.
   - Preserve unaffected task titles and wave positions. Correct the affected
     Tests placement using this evidence:
     FAIL (1 findings)
     command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token
     > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`
     - Task 1: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json

   In-flight:
   - doc/specs/report-runner.md
   - doc/plans/report-runner.md
   ```
   Then follow the parent’s required checks. Fixed observations: `PLAN WRITTEN`, then parent `PASS`, with no unrelated failure.

7. **Finalize once, in order.** Narrate the final `read` of the amended plan, without completing a phase or initializing tracking. Reopen the anchor-changed, previously complete Task 1 as `in_progress`. Preserve all unaffected tracker entries. Commit spec and plan together only after that finalization. The existing amend and this retry remain one batch; there is no ledger.

8. **Audit and undo.** Use an `amend:` subject covering both applied items. Preserve the first item’s existing audit and record `replay` as **`granted`**, including its evidence and the granting sentence. A later human-selected option would instead be audited as **`accepted`** or **`alt-n`**. Do not invent a human acceptance for this grant-applied retry.

   To undo, revert the single batch commit. Then read the grant from the pre-revert HEAD, compare it with the reverted working-tree value, and preserve the applicable consent value through Standing grants before re-entering the amendment surface. No phase is completed.

## Independent ineligible-row variants

9. **U — untracked planned test.** Reset to the pre-restore state. The added `tests/report-new.test.mjs` is `??`, a planned `Create:`/`Test:` path, and its membership check prints nothing. The **entire row is ineligible**: restore none of the original three paths. Render the writing-plans step-6 exit naming every dirty path and asking the human to commit, discard, or move them; do not partially restore or re-dispatch over unresolved dirt.

10. **P — protected path.** Reset independently. Adding the tracked spec makes the entire row ineligible because it is protected. The same applies to the plan or another In-flight path. Again, **none of the original three paths may be restored**; hand the whole row to the human through the step-6 exit.

11. **R — redraw before restoration.** Reset independently. The changed FAIL demands refund-record auditing, altering Goal and acceptance criteria. Before any restore, preserve the current batch in a commit, hand dirty paths through step 6 without restoration, then take the redraw route. Keep the worktree and spec; clear the task plan tracking, reset/start brainstorm tracking, remove the plan and identified loop ledger if present, and resume brainstorming at step 4. Do not treat this as the Tests retry or use the amendment grant to bypass redraw approval.

## Equivalent plain-jj restore

12. After equivalent eligibility checks, one intended workspace-root-anchored restore is:
   ```bash
   jj -R /tmp/report-worktree restore -- 'root:"eval/report-runner/report.md"'
   ```
   `-R` selects the repository; it does not root a relative fileset against the workspace. Use jj restoration instead of—not alongside—the git checkout path.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved: After keeps every fact Before kept. Both outputs run the three ls-files tracked/protected checks, narrate exactly three worktree-targeted `git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "<path>"` commands before applying the retry, preserve audit.log and the In-flight spec/plan, give the `root:` fileset jj equivalent with the -R caveat, attribute through the amended #tests anchor and the changed HEAD Tests line, hold the item with verbatim FAIL/row evidence and `accept`/Tests, re-read the grant and print the `amended the spec:` line without a menu, re-dispatch with an Amend-only block quoting the evidence plus both In-flight paths, finalize read → tracker reopen → one `amend:` commit with `granted` and the quoted granting sentence, explain accepted/alt-n and revert, route U/P whole-row to step 6 with no partial restore, and in R commit as-is and hand paths to step 6 before any restore with no retry item or re-dispatch. After additionally makes the two-item budget/repeated-evidence check (M4) visibly precede eligibility and restoration (M5-M6), states the no-general-cleanup rule explicitly, and spells out the `custom(<effect>)` record and the revert's effect on the retry, which delivers the Change without displacing any existing fact; the only minor wobble is U's note that SHA/exit are 'shown as missing', which is harmless but could simply say the row's values are rendered as supplied.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and fixes the one Before lost: in Before's variant U the sentence "Hand the row and protected In-flight work to the human-facing step-6 exit for commit, discard, or move" turns the spec/plan In-flight paths into cleanup targets even though they are not in the dirtied row, which fails the protected fact; After's U/P wording ("Render the writing-plans step-6 exit naming every dirty path and asking the human to commit, discard, or move them; do not partially restore or re-dispatch") scopes the exit to the row only and names step 6 explicitly in both U and P. The main trace, grant/dispatch/commit ordering, the jj root: fileset and the R variant all hold in both outputs; After is slightly more explicit in R ("Do not treat this as the Tests retry") and in P (naming the step-6 exit rather than "the same applies"), which is the wording to keep. Two small things worth tightening in After without risking any fact: say outright that both In-flight documents are preserved alongside audit.log in the main restore step (currently only implied by "outside this row"), and state in the undo paragraph that reverting the one commit removes the retry together with the original amendment, as Before did, so the commit fact's revert clause reads unambiguously.
